scope: Runtime: refit the background model by distance travelled instead of every frame
problem: TunnelBackground construction measured 40.3 ms on 72590 points - 33 per cent of a 123 ms frame, the largest single cost in the pipeline - rebuilt from scratch every frame as about 22 overlapping 30 m windows x 3 planes x 120 RANSAC iterations.
why_reuse_is_correct_here: the model's own contract is points claimed by observed LONGITUDINAL surfaces - lining, walls, ducts, bed - and those run parallel to travel, so their sensor-frame plane equations barely change between consecutive frames, which are a fraction of a metre apart. The validity of the model is a spatial property, so the refit criterion is distance travelled, not frames: a stopped train needs no refit at all.
implementation: `background_refit_travel_m`: reuse the cached model until the pose has advanced that far, then refit. Skipping the CONSTRUCTION is what saves the time - an earlier attempt disabled only the attachment and still paid the 40 ms, which the measurements showed immediately.

measured.statuses: identical on both recordings at both travel limits: 59 unresolved_obstacle on roundT_doubleT, and candidate 1 / unresolved 7 / obstacle 52 on doubleT_obstacle
measured.reading: distance-based reuse beats frame-count reuse (111.1 vs 119.2 on the tunnel recording) because it refits on demand, and it is the criterion with a physical meaning

trade_off_stated: a stale model can mis-remove the bed on a grade: at 1 m of travel and the measured 0.5 per cent bed pitch the offset error is about 5 mm, against the 25 mm fit distance, so the 1.0 m limit keeps a margin; at 2 m it is 10 mm and the metrics did not change either, but the smaller limit is the one with room to spare
pending_gate: the full 1460-frame measured-pattern panel with the 1.0 m limit: it must hold event recall 0.8021, matched IoU 0.8223 and zero negative episodes, and the recordings must keep the labelled obstacle at 52 of 52

gate_in_flight.why_a_prefixed_gate: the full 1460-frame panel was cancelled at 790 frames on a loaded machine. Subsetting the case grid is invalid - it shifts the seeds, the mistake recorded in results/sparse-range-recall-20260919.json - so the gate keeps the identical case list and seed and takes only the FIRST THREE frames per case, which are a prefix of the same seeded frame stream.
gate_in_flight.criterion: event recall, matched IoU, precision and zero negative episodes must match the off arm's
gate_in_flight.decision_it_authorises: setting background_refit_travel_m: 1.0 in configs/detector-native.json, i.e. turning the measured 15-27 per cent runtime win into the shipped default

gate_result_and_enablement.gate: prefixed A/B on the identical case list and seed, first 3 frames per case, 438 frames per arm. Every metric identical: tp 182, fn 106, fp 40, precision 0.8198, event recall 0.7917, matched IoU 0.8114, distance MAE 0.00087 m, negative episode rate 0.0, and recall by range unchanged from 10 to 300 m. Wall time per arm 124.4 s -> 103.0 s, i.e. 17 per cent on a run that includes the first frames where nothing can be reused.

enabled_in_the_shipped_recipe.infrastructure_continuity: enabled - the object-chain filter, whose own gate was byte-identical on the full 1460-frame panel; the shipped recipe had never carried it, which is now closed

shipped_recipe_measured.roundT_doubleT: 130.7 -> 114.4 ms (12 per cent faster), statuses identical
shipped_recipe_measured.doubleT_obstacle: 143.4 -> 105.9 ms (26 per cent faster), statuses identical, labelled obstacle preserved 52 of 52
shipped_recipe_measured.objects: roundT 15041 -> 13486, doubleT 14159 -> 15200 with unresolved 1754 -> 2133: relations shift slightly because a fresher model segments context slightly differently, while every frame decision is unchanged

gate_result_and_enablement.what_this_changes_for_the_case: runtime is a scored criterion (latency, frame rate, real-time stability) and the demo plays a bag in real time; a quarter of the frame time back is the difference between about 8 Hz and the real-time regime on the stand's eight cores

correction_of_the_attribution.what_was_wrong: the cadence's effect was reported as 12 and 26 per cent by comparing 130.7/143.4 against 114.4/105.9. Those runs differed in more than the cadence: the earlier one also had four registration threads instead of eight and no object-chain filter.
correction_of_the_attribution.true_effect: nothing on roundT_doubleT and about 4 per cent on doubleT_obstacle

also_corrected.object_chain_filter: costs about 9 per cent (122.2/134.7 -> 133.6/146.8), not free as implied
also_corrected.registration_threads: return 14 and 25 per cent (133.6/146.8 -> 114.6/110.7), not the 5.4 measured before the chain filter existed

correction_of_the_attribution.consequence: with the cadence worth a few per cent and the cost being the backend-equivalence guarantee, keeping the key off is better supported than it looked when the effect was overstated
